A1.justification: Both PDFs describe VaRDASS and contain readable main text, figures, tables, algorithms, equations, and Appendices A–D. Relocated and reformatted material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original variance simulations, algorithm comparisons, and adaptation experiments on Camelyon17, Humpbacks, and Spawrious, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 reports original experiments on four datasets, alongside variance simulations, runtime measurements, reclustering sensitivity results, and appendix breakdowns.

M1.justification: The MMD/CORAL stratification objectives, dynamically weighted kernel clustering, greedy assignment algorithm, and periodic reclustering procedure remain unchanged. The default T = 100 is relocated into the experimental settings, not replaced.

E1.justification: Section 3 adds Office-Home: 65-category object classification across Art, Clipart, Product, and Real World images, evaluated over 12 transfers. This substantially extends task and visual-domain coverage beyond the retained medical, acoustic, and dog-breed benchmarks.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds CDAN + SDAT and CDAN + ELS while removing AFN. The other UDA baselines and the main sampling comparators remain, making this a targeted revision of the comparison set.

E3.justification: Section 3 changes the batch-size search from k drawn as 2^Uniform(3,5.5) to 2^Uniform(3,7). Figure 4 extends testing from k = 40 to 256. New protocols evaluate final accuracy across five T values and aggregate wall-clock times across splits, hyperparameters, repeats, and both adaptation losses.

E4.justification: The component ablation now covers substantially larger batches. New Table 4 tests whether reclustering frequency affects final accuracy, supplementing the retained variance-trajectory analysis. New Table 3 compares computational costs across samplers and datasets. These additions materially expand practical robustness and efficiency analysis.

E5.justification: Section 3 changes the stated number of seeded experimental repetitions from three to five. Both versions describe varying hyperparameter, initialization, and split seeds and report accuracy means with standard errors; no new significance-testing framework is introduced.

E6.justification: Accuracy results are extensively updated under revised settings: MMD + VaRDASS changes from 90.4±1.5 to 92.0±0.5 on Humpbacks and from 72.4±2.2 to 71.6±2.2 on Spawrious. These are not identical-setting performance changes. Office-Home, runtime, T-sensitivity, and baseline-by-split results are added. Appendix C omits the previous splitwise ERM sampler ablations; Appendix D values remain identical.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, Lemma 1, Theorems 1–4, and derivations are unchanged. Appendices A and B retain the same proofs and equations despite moving to later pages.

C1.justification: The central claims remain specialized variance reduction for UDA, conditional optimality of the MMD stratification objective, and improved discrepancy estimation and target accuracy. Changing three benchmarks to four expands supporting evidence without redefining the core contribution.

C2.justification: v1 calls the post-training discrepancy analysis inconclusive and suggests a noise-floor explanation. v2 interprets the identical appendix results as indicating optimization stabilization rather than deeper minima. It also adds interpretations concerning T robustness, computational overhead, and diminishing kernel-clustering benefits at larger batches. Section 4 limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 newly supplies wall-clock training times and their aggregation procedure in Table 3, and revises the documented batch-size search range. Architecture, optimizer, kernel, training budget, and algorithmic trial settings remain documented as before; no new code or data access instructions appear.

R1.justification: References are added for SDAT, ELS, Office-Home, Napoli and White's 2024 data-balancing work, and their 2026 follow-up; the AFN reference is removed. Brief discussion connects diverse sampling to balancing and introduces the follow-up. The existing 2024 citation becomes 2024b without changing the cited work.

P1.justification: Experimental discussion receives localized revisions, Section 5.1 adds a short follow-up paragraph, and publication and review information is added. The principal section order, appendix organization, and most method and theory prose are retained.

P2.justification: Empirical displays are substantially reorganized: Tables 1–2 expand, runtime and T-sensitivity tables are added, and Figure 4 receives extended axes and revised styling. Appendix C changes from stacked split blocks to method-by-split matrices and adds Office-Home. The other figures and Appendix D table retain their content.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens practical evaluation by supplying previously missing runtime measurements and final-accuracy sensitivity to reclustering frequency (Tables 3–4). Broader task coverage, revised adversarial comparisons, and additional repetitions strengthen empirical validation. These gains outweigh the less cautious mechanism interpretation of unchanged Appendix D results, which does not itself establish that trajectory stabilization causes the accuracy benefits.
